kinds.distance: a separation, not an object size
kinds.scale: a derived or theoretical characteristic length

statuses.upper_limit: only an upper bound is known
statuses.lower_limit: only a lower bound is known
statuses.theoretical: follows from accepted theory but not directly measured
statuses.approximate: typical/representative value with wide natural spread
statuses.contested: existence or value disputed in the literature

formula_namespace: formulas are Python expressions evaluated in check.py NS() (constants in SI)

objects.name: Planck length
objects.source: CODATA 2022 (Mohr et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002, 2025; physics.nist.gov/constants)
objects.description: Length built from G, ħ and c; where quantum gravity is expected to matter. Not proven to be a pixel.

objects.name: Compton–Schwarzschild crossing (√2 Planck lengths)
objects.description: Where a mass would be its own black hole and its own quantum wavelength at once.

objects.name: String length (if strings exist)
objects.uncertainty: model-dependent; could be 1e-35 to much larger
objects.source: textbook value (e.g. Zwiebach, A First Course in String Theory, 2009); flagged
objects.description: Typical size assumed for fundamental strings in string theory. No experimental evidence exists.

objects.name: Grand-unification scale (ħc / 10^16 GeV)
objects.source: textbook value (GUT scale ~1e16 GeV from running couplings; PDG GUT review); flagged
objects.description: Distance at which forces might merge into one, in grand unified theories. Untested.

objects.name: De Broglie wavelength of the "Oh-My-God" cosmic ray (3.2e20 eV)
objects.description: Highest-energy particle ever recorded; its quantum wavelength is far below anything a collider reaches.

objects.name: Wavelength of the most energetic photon seen (1.4 PeV)
objects.description: A gamma ray from the Cygnus region; the shortest light wavelength ever detected.

objects.name: Distance resolved by LHC collisions (ħc / 2 TeV)
objects.source: CERN LHC Run 3 at 13.6 TeV; parton energies ~TeV
objects.description: Smallest distances probed directly; set by the energy of colliding quarks and gluons.

objects.name: Upper limit on quark size
objects.description: No quark size has been seen; if quarks have one it is smaller than this.

objects.name: Upper limit on electron size
objects.source: LEP e+e− contact-interaction limits, PDG review "Searches for quark and lepton compositeness"
objects.description: The electron behaves as a point: scattering shows no structure down to at least this scale.

objects.name: Top quark reduced Compton wavelength
objects.source: Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics (Navas et al., Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001, 2024)
objects.description: Heaviest known particle; its quantum wavelength is tiny because its mass is huge.

objects.name: Higgs boson reduced Compton wavelength
objects.source: Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics (Navas et al., Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001, 2024)
objects.description: Quantum length of the Higgs boson, discovered at the LHC in 2012.

objects.name: Z boson reduced Compton wavelength (weak-force range)
objects.source: Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics (Navas et al., Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001, 2024)
objects.description: Roughly how far the weak nuclear force reaches before fading away.

objects.name: W boson reduced Compton wavelength
objects.source: Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics (Navas et al., Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001, 2024)
objects.description: Quantum length of the W boson, which carries the charge-changing weak force.

objects.name: Proton reduced Compton wavelength
objects.source: CODATA 2022 (Mohr et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002, 2025; physics.nist.gov/constants)
objects.description: Quantum length of the proton; smaller than the proton's measured charge radius.

objects.name: Proton charge radius

objects.name: Pion reduced Compton wavelength (range of the nuclear force)

objects.name: Helium-4 nucleus (alpha particle) charge radius

objects.name: Muon reduced Compton wavelength

objects.description: Quantum length of the muon, the electron's 207-times-heavier cousin.

objects.name: Deuteron charge radius
objects.source: CODATA 2022 (Mohr et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002, 2025; physics.nist.gov/constants)

objects.name: Milky Way dark matter halo
objects.description: Invisible dark matter extends far beyond the visible stars and dominates the mass.

objects.name: Distance to the Andromeda galaxy (M31)
objects.source: McConnachie, AJ 144, 4 (2012); Riess et al., ApJ 745, 156 (2012)
objects.description: The most distant object easily seen with the naked eye: 2.5 million light-years.

objects.name: Local Group of galaxies
objects.description: The Milky Way, Andromeda and about 100 smaller galaxies bound together.

objects.name: Rich galaxy cluster (e.g. Coma)
objects.source: textbook value (e.g. Kubo et al., ApJ 671, 1466 (2007) for Coma); flagged
objects.description: Largest gravitationally bound structures: thousands of galaxies in hot gas and dark matter.

objects.name: Distance to the Virgo Cluster
objects.description: Nearest large galaxy cluster, at the heart of our local supercluster.

objects.name: Typical cosmic void
objects.source: textbook value (e.g. Sutter et al., ApJ 761, 44 (2012) void catalogues); flagged
objects.description: Nearly empty bubbles between the filaments of the cosmic web.

objects.name: Boötes Void
objects.source: Kirshner et al., ApJL 248, L57 (1981); flagged size
objects.description: One of the largest known voids, with only a few dozen galaxies.

objects.name: Scale of cosmic homogeneity
objects.description: Above this size the universe looks statistically the same everywhere.

objects.name: Baryon acoustic oscillation scale (sound horizon)
objects.description: Frozen sound waves from the early universe set this preferred spacing between galaxies.

objects.name: Laniakea Supercluster
objects.description: Our home supercluster: 100,000 galaxies flowing toward a common basin.

objects.name: Sloan Great Wall
objects.description: A vast sheet of galaxies; one of the largest structures in the cosmic web.

objects.name: Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall (contested)
objects.source: Horváth et al., A&A 561, L12 (2014); flagged
objects.description: Claimed clustering of gamma-ray bursts; may be a statistical fluke.

objects.name: Hubble radius c/H₀ (H₀ = 67.4)
objects.description: Distance at which galaxies recede at light speed today. Not a physical edge.

objects.name: Cosmic event horizon (comoving, today)
objects.source: Planck Collaboration 2018 VI, A&A 641, A6 (2020); computed in check.py
objects.description: Light emitted today beyond this distance will never reach us.

objects.name: Distance to the CMB last-scattering surface (comoving)
objects.source: Planck Collaboration 2018 VI, A&A 641, A6 (2020); computed in check.py
objects.description: Where the cosmic microwave background light we see today set out, 380,000 years after the Big Bang.

objects.name: Observable universe (particle horizon radius)
objects.source: Planck Collaboration 2018 VI, A&A 641, A6 (2020); Davis & Lineweaver, PASA 21, 97 (2004)
objects.description: Farthest distance from which light could have reached us in 13.8 billion years. Mass is ordinary matter only.

objects.name: Observable universe (diameter)
objects.source: Planck Collaboration 2018 VI, A&A 641, A6 (2020); Davis & Lineweaver, PASA 21, 97 (2004)
objects.description: The whole sphere of space we can, in principle, see. Not the whole universe.

objects.name: Lower limit on the curvature radius of space
objects.source: Planck Collaboration 2018 VI, A&A 641, A6 (2020) (Ω_k = 0.0007 ± 0.0019 with BAO)
objects.description: If space is curved at all, it curves on scales at least this large.
